goal: Re-review the /dashboard skeleton-flash fix after iteration 2: confirm my three iteration-1 warnings are genuinely resolved in the live code, apply fresh scrutiny to the code that did not exist in iteration 1 (errorUnlessAlreadyLoaded, the always-revalidate effect, src/db/dashboard.ts, the BetaBanner prop change), and answer verifier's explicit question about whether a third live-browser probe is warranted.
summary: Read the working-tree diff against HEAD myself (git diff HEAD on route.ts / page.tsx / BetaBanner.tsx plus a full read of the two untracked new files) rather than trusting any handoff prose, re-ran typecheck and both dashboard test files green from the current tree, and ran my own throwaway DOM probe (created, run, deleted, git status re-confirmed clean) to answer the two questions the task put to me empirically instead of by reasoning. ALL THREE ITERATION-1 WARNINGS ARE GENUINELY RESOLVED. (W1 type drift) src/db/dashboard.ts owns DashboardData and buildDashboardPayload(uid, email): Promise<DashboardData>; page.tsx:4,41 and route.ts:23,42 are the only two production callers and both go through it. The route is now type-checked, though by a different mechanism than I proposed: the builder's explicit Promise<DashboardData> return type does the enforcement at the declaration, so NextResponse.json(payload) is guarded without a call-site annotation. That is equivalent and slightly better than my suggested fix. The duelStats narrowing side effect is safe -- I re-checked the two consumers independently of verifier: web DashboardBody types the response as the same DashboardData and reads only the four counters, and mobile AppDataContext declares its own DashboardData with no duelStats field; separately confirmed mobile ProfileScreen.tsx:195,235 is the one reader of user.email and that field is unchanged (decoded.email ?? ""), including the anonymous-user empty-string case which both of its call sites already treat as falsy. (W2 BetaBanner layout shift) DashboardBody.tsx:193-202 now has no `token &&` gate at all -- both arms of the betaJoined ternary are decided by server-known data, so whichever element will show is in the first server-rendered frame and nothing inserts itself above WalletCard later. BetaBanner.tsx:16,45,101 pushes the token dependency down to the Join button only, guarded twice (disabled attribute plus an `if (!token) return;` early return). (W3 no revalidation path) There is no `initialData !== null` guard anywhere in DashboardBody; the effect at :111-115 gates only on authLoading/user/token. I additionally confirmed a code-level reason this actually fires on a history-traversal restore, which nobody has written down: AuthProvider lives in app/layout.tsx:111, above the route segment, so it does NOT unmount on a client-side back/forward navigation -- authLoading is already false and token already populated when DashboardBody remounts, so the effect's auth gate cannot swallow or delay the restore-time revalidation. FRESH SCRUTINY OF THE NEW CODE. errorUnlessAlreadyLoaded is correct in every case I could construct: seeded-success then failure keeps content (covered by the existing test); null-initialData first-fetch failure still shows the error card (covered); and the case nobody had tested -- a SECOND background failure after a first revalidation already succeeded -- I proved myself, by mounting the real component, resolving fetch #1 with fresh data, then changing the token to force a second revalidation that rejects: the fresh 9-1 record stayed painted and no role=alert appeared. That probe also confirmed the effect does re-arm on a token change (2 fetches), i.e. a ~1h Firebase token refresh triggers another revalidation exactly as the pre-fix code did. On the identical-data re-render question: I mounted the real component, let the revalidation resolve with a deep-equal but brand-new object, and asserted DOM node identity -- the FreeClimbCard <section> (which carries animate-climbEnter / animate-climbGroundRise) is the SAME Node object before and after, the selected tab survives, and document.activeElement is unchanged. So the new object identity causes a reconciliation-only re-render: no remount, therefore no CSS entrance-animation replay, no loss of the replay sections' local expanded/toast state, no scroll or focus disturbance. There is no flicker to flag. TWO WARNINGS, NEITHER BLOCKING. (a) The always-revalidate design is NOT cost-neutral versus the pre-fix baseline, contrary to the framing in the software-engineer handoff -- I traced it rather than deferring. buildDashboardPayload issues 7 Prisma queries (user.findUnique; getUserFreeClimbRecord = 1 findUnique + 2 climbRecord.count; climbRun.findMany; duelStats.findUnique; duel.findMany). Pre-fix a dashboard view cost 7 (one client fetch). Iteration 1 cost 7 (server only). Iteration 2 costs 14 on every server-populated view -- the server render AND the mount revalidation each run the full builder, which means the unbounded category-wide climbRecord.count over climb_records now runs twice per dashboard view. Real, measurable, on the most-visited authed page, and nobody measured it; not critical because there is no correctness failure and the alternative was a proven HIGH defect. (b) src/db/dashboard.ts is the only file in src/db/ that imports from src/components/ -- it pulls four types out of "use client" React component modules, inverting the dependency direction for the lowest layer in the app. Type-only and erased today (I confirmed isolatedModules:true would reject a bare type re-export, and there is no value import), but the edge is unenforced: this repo has no server-only guard and no eslint boundary rule, and DashboardBody.tsx already re-exports the type back across that boundary. Plus three info items: the DashboardData re-export at DashboardBody.tsx:37 has exactly one consumer and it is a test; the silent-failure-after-success behaviour is a genuine (and good) UX delta from pre-fix that belongs in the PR description; and the Join button is disabled without explanation and out of the tab order for the token window. Untouched parts have not regressed -- I diffed DashboardBody's JSX line-for-line against the original page.tsx body preserved in the working-tree diff and it is identical except the beta block, metadata is still at page.tsx:7-9, and every changed control has a non-test caller except the one re-export named above. VERIFIER'S THIRD-PROBE QUESTION: no, a third live-browser probe is not warranted -- reasoning in feedback[0].

findings.issue: The always-revalidate-on-every-mount design doubles the cost of a dashboard view, and that is a real regression versus the pre-fix baseline rather than the neutral trade the software-engineer handoff describes. Traced precisely: buildDashboardPayload issues 7 Prisma queries per call -- prisma.user.findUnique, getUserFreeClimbRecord (1 climbRecord.findUnique + 2 climbRecord.count), getUserClimbReplays (1 findMany), getDuelStats (1 findUnique), getRecentDuelsForUser (1 findMany). Pre-change a /dashboard view ran the builder once (the client fetch). Iteration 1 ran it once (server only, client fetch suppressed). Iteration 2 runs it TWICE on every server-populated view: once in the page's server render, then again via GET /api/dashboard from the mount revalidation -- which always fires, because the effect has no way to tell an SSR-fresh payload from a bfcache-restored one. The expensive part is `prisma.climbRecord.count({ where: { category_slug: FREE_STACK_SLUG } })`, an unbounded COUNT over climb_records that grows with the leaderboard and now runs twice per dashboard view, plus a second rank COUNT alongside it. Not critical: no correctness failure, and the only alternative on record (iteration 1) carried a proven HIGH staleness defect, so shipping this is still the right call -- but the cost is real, is on the most-visited authenticated page, and no agent in either iteration measured it.
findings.fix: Cheapest fix with an in-repo precedent and no freshness tradeoff: the total-climbers COUNT is category-global, not per-user, so wrap it the way this codebase already wraps its other category-global leaderboard read -- `unstable_cache(..., ['freeStackClimberCount'], { revalidate: 60, tags: [LEADERBOARD_CACHE_TAG] })`, mirroring app/src/db/climb.ts:151. (Note app/src/db/climb.ts:186-197 getGlobalClimbStats already computes exactly this COUNT for the landing page; the two could share one cached read.) If the team instead wants to remove the duplicate call entirely, add a server-stamped `resolvedAt: number` to DashboardData and skip the mount revalidation when `Date.now() - initialData.resolvedAt` is both >= 0 and < ~5000ms -- an SSR-fresh payload is always within that window and a history-traversal-restored one never is, which is precisely the distinction the defect needs. Either way, measure /dashboard server render time and /api/dashboard p95 under a realistic climb_records row count before picking.

findings.issue: Dependency direction is inverted for the new module, and it is the only place in the codebase that does this. src/db/dashboard.ts imports FreeClimbData, ClimbReplayItem, DuelRecordData and DuelReplayItem from four files under src/components/Dashboard/, all of which are "use client" React component modules. I grepped src/db/ -- no other db module imports from src/components. The lowest layer now depends on the highest, and the db layer already owns equivalent types it declined to use (ClimbReplaySummary in src/db/climb.ts:248-253 is structurally identical to ClimbReplayItem; RecentDuelItem in src/db/duel.ts:701 is a superset of DuelReplayItem). The edge is type-only and fully erased today -- I confirmed tsconfig has isolatedModules:true, which makes a bare `export { DashboardData }` a compile error, so the DashboardBody.tsx:37 re-export cannot silently become a value edge -- but nothing else enforces it: this repo has no `server-only` import anywhere and eslint.config.mjs has no no-restricted-imports / boundaries rule. A future maintainer adding, say, a shared formatter value import from one of those four component modules into this db module would pull React client components into the Prisma module graph server-side, and there is no build-time gate that would catch it.
findings.fix: Declare DashboardData against the db layer's own types instead of reaching up into the components: use ClimbReplaySummary (src/db/climb.ts) for `replays`, RecentDuelItem (src/db/duel.ts) for `recentDuels`, and move or re-declare the small FreeClimbData / DuelRecordData shapes in the db layer -- the components accept them structurally, so no component file needs to change. Optionally make the boundary enforced rather than conventional by adding `import "server-only";` to the top of app/src/db/client.ts, which turns an accidental client import of any db module into a build failure instead of a silent Prisma bundle.

findings.issue: The `export type { DashboardData } from "../../src/db/dashboard";` re-export has exactly one consumer in the whole repo and it is a test. I grepped: page.tsx imports the type from src/db/dashboard, route.ts imports the builder from src/db/dashboard, and the sibling test tests/components/dashboardBodyRevalidate.test.tsx:39 already imports it from src/db/dashboard -- only dashboardBody.test.tsx:25 goes through DashboardBody. So this is an exported symbol whose only caller is a test, which is the shape .claude/rules/testing.md tells us to look for. Line 26 also imports the same symbol from the same module that line 37 re-exports, so the module is named twice.
findings.fix: Point dashboardBody.test.tsx:25 at `../../src/db/dashboard` for the type, exactly as its sibling revalidate test already does, then delete the line-37 re-export and its comment block. Line 26's `import type` stays and remains the file's single reference to the module.

findings.issue: Undocumented behaviour delta that belongs in the PR description rather than in the code. errorUnlessAlreadyLoaded keys on `prev.status === 'success'`, not on whether the content came from the server -- so it also suppresses the error card for a failure that follows a SUCCESSFUL CLIENT fetch, which is a path the pre-fix code surfaced. Pre-fix: null initialData -> fetch succeeds -> an hour later the token refreshes, that refetch fails, and the user saw the 'Network error. Please refresh.' card. Now they see their last-known numbers with no indication they are stale. I proved this transition against the real component (mount, resolve fetch #1 with fresh data, change token to force fetch #2, reject it): the fresh record stayed painted and no role=alert appeared. This is the right default for a background revalidation -- replacing correct content with an error card is worse -- and it is what makes the fix safe, so no code change. But it is a silent-failure mode that no test names as intentional and no handoff mentions.
findings.fix: No code change. Call it out in the PR description: after any successful load, /dashboard fails silently and shows last-known data. If the team later wants a signal, the smallest version is a non-blocking staleness marker (a muted 'updated Xm ago' or a small retry affordance) driven off a lastSuccessAt timestamp -- never a state transition that unmounts the painted content.

findings.issue: Residual UX cost of the W2 fix, far smaller than the layout shift it replaced. For the ~100-500ms until the Firebase session resolves (and permanently in the rare case where the server cookie is valid but the client session never resolves), the banner's primary CTA renders `disabled` with no explanation -- just disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed. A native `disabled` button is also removed from the tab order, so a fast keyboard user tabbing through the first painted frame skips 'Join beta' and the focus order changes under them when the token lands. This is the correct trade versus shifting the whole content column, so it is not a regression to fix now.
findings.fix: If the team wants the last 5%: swap `disabled` for `aria-disabled={token === null}` plus an aria-describedby pointing at visually-hidden text ('available once your session loads'), keeping the existing `if (!token) return;` guard in handleSubmit as the real gate. That keeps the control in the tab order and explains itself, instead of silently swallowing the click.

findings.issue: Staging hazard carried forward from iteration 1 and now larger. Four files in this change are untracked -- app/app/dashboard/DashboardBody.tsx, app/src/db/dashboard.ts, app/tests/components/dashboardBody.test.tsx and app/tests/components/dashboardBodyRevalidate.test.tsx -- while app/app/dashboard/layout.tsx's deletion is unstaged. A `git commit -a` would capture the deletion, the page.tsx rewrite and the route.ts import change but silently drop all four new files, producing a commit that cannot build (page.tsx and route.ts both import src/db/dashboard).
findings.fix: Integrator: stage explicitly -- `git add app/app/dashboard/DashboardBody.tsx app/src/db/dashboard.ts app/tests/components/dashboardBody.test.tsx app/tests/components/dashboardBodyRevalidate.test.tsx` plus `git rm app/app/dashboard/layout.tsx` -- and confirm `git status --short` shows no remaining `??` under app/ before committing. Branch is claude/amazing-pascal-xjxhdl; per context/git.md open a PR against main rather than pushing main.

feedback.message: Verifier's explicit question (verifier-2026-09-20T144543Z learnings[2]): is the DOM mutation test plus two prior live-browser probes enough for a HIGH finding's fix, or is a third live-browser confirmation warranted before sign-off? My answer is NO, a third probe is not warranted, and the reason is coverage rather than probe count. The evidence on record is not three repetitions of one experiment -- it is two experiments that cover complementary halves of the claim. qa-acceptance's iteration-1 probe plus its Next.js 16.3.4 source reading established the PRECONDITION (history traversal restores a cached RSC segment with no fresh request and deliberately ignores staleTimes.dynamic). software-engineer's iteration-2 probe established the MECHANISM in a real browser on this app's real production build, and crucially did it as a controlled A/B with the iteration-1 logic rendered side by side from the same server prop -- the control stayed stale while the fixed logic healed, which rules out 'some unrelated build difference fixed it', the single most likely way a browser probe lies. The one genuine gap in that probe is that its fixed component was a REIMPLEMENTATION of the effect logic, not the real DashboardBody -- exactly the failure mode .claude/rules/testing.md warns about ('a diverged copy will assert the inverse of production and still pass'). Verifier's mutation test closes precisely that gap, on the real component, for both load-bearing mechanisms. Union of the two = real browser mechanism + real production component. A third repetition of the same browser probe would add ~nothing. I also closed the one residual way the real component could diverge from the probe copy, by reading code rather than running anything: the probe copy had no auth gate, whereas the real effect early-returns on authLoading/user/token, so in principle the revalidation could be swallowed or delayed on a restore. It cannot -- AuthProvider is mounted in app/layout.tsx:111, above the route segment, so it does not unmount on a client-side back/forward navigation; authLoading is already false and token already populated when DashboardBody remounts, and the effect fires on its first pass. If anyone still wants belt-and-braces, the useful extra experiment is NOT a third run of the same probe but a different one: a probe route that mounts the REAL DashboardBody with a stub payload. That is the only remaining uncovered combination. I do not think it is worth blocking on.
feedback.action: verifier/qa-acceptance: proceed without a third live-browser probe. If extra confidence is ever wanted on this pattern, mount the real component in the probe route instead of re-running the same copy-based A/B.

learnings.insight: The background-revalidate cure for the seed-and-suppress staleness bug is not cost-neutral, and it is easy to describe as if it were. The natural framing -- 'the client fetch runs on every mount, exactly like the pre-server-render version' -- is true about the CLIENT fetch and completely misses that the server read is additive. On /dashboard the payload builder is 7 Prisma queries, so a server-populated view went from 7 (pre-fix, or iteration 1) to 14, and the two unbounded category-wide climbRecord.count queries now run twice per view. Three agents across two iterations reviewed this change and none of them counted the queries; the cost only becomes visible if you open the builder and add up what each read actually issues rather than counting 'one Promise.all'.
learnings.action: When a page converts to server-resolved initialData AND keeps a mount revalidation, state the per-view query count before and after in the handoff. If the builder contains any unbounded COUNT or aggregate, cache the parts that are not per-user (this repo's precedent: unstable_cache with a revalidate + tag, src/db/climb.ts:151) in the same change, or add a server-stamped resolvedAt so the mount revalidation can skip a payload that is only milliseconds old while still firing for a bfcache-restored one.

learnings.insight: Extracting a shared payload builder into src/db/ is the right de-duplication, but the payload's field types usually live in the UI components that consume them, so the extraction quietly drags src/db (lowest layer) into a dependency on src/components (highest layer) -- here src/db/dashboard.ts became the only file in src/db/ importing from src/components/, pulling four types out of "use client" modules. It is invisible in review because the imports are `import type` and erase cleanly, and every bundle grep comes back clean. The db layer frequently already owns an equivalent type (ClimbReplaySummary vs the component's ClimbReplayItem, RecentDuelItem vs DuelReplayItem) and the components accept it structurally, so the inversion buys nothing. This repo has no `server-only` import and no eslint boundaries rule, so the edge is convention-only.
learnings.action: When extracting a shared payload builder, type its interface from the data layer's own types and let the components accept them structurally; never import component types downward into src/db. If you must, make the boundary enforced rather than conventional in the same change -- `import "server-only";` at the top of the db entry module turns an accidental client import into a build failure.

learnings.insight: Two questions that usually get answered by React reasoning -- 'does a revalidation with deep-equal-but-new-identity data cause a visible re-render / animation replay / state or focus loss?' and 'is the Nth failure after a success still handled correctly?' -- are both cheap to answer empirically on the real component with a throwaway happy-dom mount, and the DOM-node-identity assertion is the crisp proof. `expect(container.querySelector(sel)).toBe(nodeCapturedBefore)` after the revalidation resolves proves no remount, which in one assertion rules out CSS entrance-animation replay, loss of children's local expanded/toast state, and scroll/focus disturbance -- none of which a snapshot or innerHTML assertion would catch. Forcing a SECOND revalidation is also easy: change the value the effect depends on (here the auth mock's token, mirroring Firebase's ~1h refresh) and re-render.
learnings.action: As a reviewer, when a change makes a component re-render with fresh object identity on a path it did not before, spend the two minutes on a throwaway mount that captures a child node before and asserts `.toBe()` after, rather than reasoning about React reconciliation in the handoff. Delete the probe and re-check `git status --short` before writing up.

learnings.insight: 'Do we need another independent confirmation?' is the wrong question; 'which halves of the claim does each existing experiment actually cover?' is the right one. For this fix the two browser probes and the mutation test were not three tries at the same thing: one established the router precondition, one established the mechanism in a real browser on the real build WITH the defective logic as an in-page control, and the third proved both mechanisms load-bearing on the REAL component -- which matters because the browser probe used a reimplementation of the effect, the exact 'diverged copy' failure mode .claude/rules/testing.md warns about. Once you decompose it that way the answer falls out: the union is covered, a repetition adds nothing, and the only uncovered combination (real component inside a real browser probe) is a different experiment, not a third run of the same one.
learnings.action: When an agent asks whether another confirmation is warranted, answer by listing what each piece of existing evidence covers and naming the uncovered combination, rather than by counting confirmations. If the uncovered combination is narrow and a code-level argument closes it (here: AuthProvider sits in the root layout, so the auth gate cannot swallow the restore-time revalidation), say so and do not spend the cycle.
